entry.title: The folklore conjecture on unbounded class-group ranks
entry.literal_statement: Let $d>1$ and $m>1$ be integers. For a number field $k$, let $\operatorname{Cl}(k)$ denote its ideal class group, let $[k:\mathbb{Q}]$ denote its degree over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $\operatorname{rk}_m\operatorname{Cl}(k)$ be the largest integer $r$ such that $(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^r$ is a subgroup of $\operatorname{Cl}(k)$. **Folklore conjecture.** The quantity $\operatorname{rk}_m\operatorname{Cl}(k)$ is unbounded as $k$ ranges over number fields satisfying $[k:\mathbb{Q}]=d$. This conjecture concerns the existence of arbitrarily large prescribed-torsion ranks in class groups within each fixed degree; it is widely believed to be true, while the survey presents geometric techniques related to constructing such examples.
entry.technical_disposition_and_next_lemma: Arbitrary fixed degree d and torsion m includes major unresolved class-group rank questions; genus-theory2-torsion instances do not settle all parameters. Next: genuinely uniform number-field construction.

entry.literal_statement:
Let $B=(0;\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)$ be any non-trivial block decomposition of even weight $N$. **Alternate odd positions conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Alt}_{\{\ell_i\mid i\text{ odd}\}}I_{\mathrm{bl}}^{\mathfrak m}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)=0.
$$

The conjecture extends the analogous alternating identity for 123-multiple zeta values to arbitrary block lengths. It is proposed after the special case suggested by Borwein, Bradley and Broadhurst; no proof or disproof is given in the source.
